primitives.name: Copyright Usage Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Copyright License The licensor grants you a copyright license for the software to do everything you might do with the software that would otherwise infringe the licensor's copyright in it for any permitted purpose.
primitives.assumptions: Usage is bounded by permitted purposes; no explicit restriction on scope beyond noncommercial.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's belief update function \( \mathcal{B}(\text{action} | \text{license}) \) and GSE's state transition \( \mathcal{S}_{\text{active}} \leftarrow \text{acceptance} \land \text{compliance} \).
layer2.telemetry: License acceptance event, usage log, compliance audit.

primitives.name: Distribution Conditional Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Distribution License The licensor grants you an additional copyright license to distribute copies of the software.
primitives.assumptions: Distribution requires adherence to changes/new works license; not independent of modification rights.

layer2.mapping: Derived from copyright kernel; GSI models as conditional probability \( P(\text{distribute} | \text{modify}) \); GSE tracks \( \mathcal{S}_{\text{distribution}} \subseteq \mathcal{S}_{\text{active}} \).
layer2.telemetry: Distribution event, change tracking, license compliance check.

primitives.name: Patent Infringement Shield
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Patent License The licensor grants you a patent license for the software that covers patent claims the licensor can license, or becomes able to license, that you would infringe by using the software.
primitives.assumptions: License is contingent upon non-infringement; defense mechanism activated by assertion of infringement.

layer2.mapping: GSI models as adversarial risk \( R_{\text{patent}} = \mathbb{E}[\text{assertion}] \cdot \mathbb{P}(\text{infringement}) \); GSE enforces \( \mathcal{S}_{\text{patent\_defense}} \).
layer2.telemetry: Patent assertion log, litigation status, license termination event.

The PolyForm NonCommercial 1.0.0 license defines a structured lattice of permissions \( \mathcal{L} \) over software usage, distribution, and modification. Each primitive forms a node in this lattice: copyright license \( \mathcal{C} \) enables general use, distribution license \( \mathcal{D} \) adds distribution rights, and patent license \( \mathcal{P} \) provides protection against patent claims. The lattice is constrained by permitted purposes, which are defined as noncommercial or specific categories such as personal, educational, or governmental use. Violation of these terms leads to immediate termination of all licenses, modeled as a failure mode \( \mathcal{F} \) in the state space \( \mathcal{S} \). The license structure exhibits a dual nature: it is both a conditional permission system and a constraint-based access control model. The interplay between \( \mathcal{C} \), \( \mathcal{D} \), and \( \mathcal{P} \) creates a hierarchical dependency graph where \( \mathcal{D} \) depends on \( \mathcal{C} \) and \( \mathcal{P} \). This lattice is embedded in a temporal logic framework where \( \Box (\text{compliance} \rightarrow \text{active}) \) governs the evolution of \( \mathcal{S} \). The license also introduces a dynamic element through its patent defense clause, which acts as a trigger for \( \mathcal{F} \) when \( \text{assertion} \rightarrow \text{infringement} \). The failure modes are thus tied to both explicit violations and implicit non-compliance, forming a robust but brittle system of conditional rights.

reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Anti-collinearity arises from the tension between \( \mathcal{C} \) and \( \mathcal{P} \): if \( \mathcal{P} \) is invoked, \( \mathcal{C} \) may become invalid. Leakage occurs when \( \mathcal{D} \) is misapplied without \( \mathcal{C} \) or \( \mathcal{P} \). Veto conditions include explicit assertion of patent infringement, which triggers immediate termination of all licenses, ensuring no cross-layer contamination of rights.
